In cross-coupling reactions (such as Suzuki, Heck, Stille, and other palladium-catalyzed reactions), the reactivity of aryl halides follows the order:

Aryl iodides > Aryl bromides > Aryl chlorides > Aryl fluorides

This order is based on the carbon-halogen bond strength, which decreases down the group in the periodic table. Aryl iodides and bromides have weaker carbon-halogen bonds, making them more reactive in oxidative addition steps that are crucial in cross-coupling reactions. Aryl fluorides have the strongest carbon-halogen bonds and are generally unreactive in most cross-coupling conditions.

Aryl astatides are not commonly used in organic synthesis due to the radioactive nature of astatine and its scarcity.

Therefore, aryl bromides and iodides are the most useful in cross-coupling reactions.
